title: remove_on_error log lines must reflect the actual cleanup outcome
answers: misleading Successfully removed warning for a file that was never created
log says removed when the path was not deleted
why does the cleanup log claim success for a missing path
body:
Symptom: Logs say a partial file was removed when it never existed or was not removed.
Root cause: mlflow/utils/file_utils.py:remove_on_error chose its message by re-checking os.path.exists(path) after cleanup, which is true for neither the never-created nor the failed-cleanup case.
Fix pattern: Pick a remover by os.path.isfile / os.path.isdir before the try; log 'Successfully removed' only right after the remover returns, and 'Failed to remove <path>: <error>' from the except. Paths that are neither regular file nor directory are logged as 'Not removing' and left alone.
Constraints: Tests in tests/utils/test_file_utils.py assert the exact list of warning messages emitted, so any new log line changes those assertions. Nonexistent paths log nothing.
applies: Changes to remove_on_error's logging or its file/directory dispatch.
says: Console logs falsely report cleanup succeeded for files that were never created.
Activity log claims partial files were removed even when deletion actually failed.
Stop showing successful cleanup messages when aborting downloads that created no files.
Failure logs should clearly indicate when temporary file deletion fails or is skipped.
search: Logging in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py:remove_on_error must accurately report cleanup outcomes by checking os.path.isfile or os.path.isdir before cleanup and logging 'Successfully removed' only immediately after removal returns. Failed deletions must log 'Failed to remove <path>: <error>' from the except block, paths neither file nor directory must be logged as 'Not removing' and left alone, and nonexistent paths must log nothing. This applies to changes to remove_on_error's logging or file/directory dispatch, where tests in tests/utils/test_file_utils.py assert the exact list of emitted warning messages.
